observations.observation: M5 passed its pinned synchronous typed component and owned-resource selection. Its stated scope excludes WASI, native async and full Component-Draft; its selected memory32/UTF-8 pin is genuine, not a missing pin.
observations.counterexample: Advertising M5's successful Rust/Wasmtime component peer as full standard WASI/Component-Draft would promote a selected sync world beyond the evidence.

observations.observation: M6 passed WI-11/WI-12/WI-16 native async paths. Its separately pinned official 0.3.0-rc-2025-09-16 clock probe is peer-only; the selected linker rejected stable 0.3.0, not silently substituted it.
observations.counterexample: Claiming M6 native async is unexecuted discards real receipts; claiming its prerelease peer-only clock is Noble-compiled stable WASI incorrectly enlarges them.

observations.observation: WI-ARCH-01 through WI-ARCH-04 separate component artifact, WIT IDL, Noble-internal semantics and host authority. WI-SAFE-03 requires full-profile boundary coverage beyond the selected M5/M6 lanes; ledger SO-01/SO-07 and other broader safety obligations remain open.
observations.counterexample: A WIT import shape or a link success by itself confers neither host authority nor assurance of malformed values, all async cancellation paths or full loader correctness.

observations.observation: S-GATE-03 permits future higher-rank features only after rules preserving safety and matching proof obligations. The current language defines rank-1 schemes only; S-VERIFY-03 forbids treating unsupported or an open proof as success. V-SAFE-04 requires declarative rules, acceptance, correspondence and affected safety theorems in release evidence.
observations.counterexample: A valid rank-1 checker theorem cannot license an unsupported higher-rank program as stable-safe; unsupported is not a proof of unsafety or a permanent feature ban.
